issues.description: The template declares the helper method singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), whereas the problem UML and the solution expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This parameter mismatch between the template and the specified design can confuse students about the intended signature and how to implement singFarmSong() (which should call a verse helper per animal).
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Farm.java to declare singFarmSongVerse with an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) to match the UML/specification and the solution. Ensure singFarmSong() iterates animals and calls singFarmSongVerse(animal).

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires Farm.animals to be a List implemented with an ArrayList and instructs initializing an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor, but the solution implements animals as a Queue<Animal> backed by a LinkedList. This attribute type/implementation mismatch between the specification and the provided solution can confuse students about the expected type for the getter/setter and which collection to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align implementation with the problem statement: declare the animals attribute as List<Animal> and initialize it as an ArrayList<> in the no-arg constructor, and make the getter/setter use List<Animal>. Alternatively, update the problem statement to accept a generic Collection/Queue implementation if Queue semantics are intended.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires the Farm to use a List implemented with an ArrayList for the animals collection, but the solution implements the animals collection as a Queue backed by a LinkedList (different type identifier). This diverges from the instructions and creates a mapping confusion: students are told to use List/ArrayList but the reference solution uses Queue/LinkedList, which may lead to uncertainty about the required collection type and the expected constructor/initialization.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement. Either (A) change the solution to use a List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() (and adjust getter/setter signatures to List<Animal>), or (B) update the problem statement to allow Queue/LinkedList and remove the explicit ArrayList requirement. Preferred: use List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>(); to match the problem instructions.
